record.prompt: Our new product photos are up to 64 megapixels. resize/pipeline.py downscales everything to 40 MP before sending it to Tamberline. Look at their changelog at https://tamberline.example/changelog and tell me whether we can drop that step.
record.final_answer:
Yes — the size limit is no longer the reason to downscale. Tamberline v2.6 (2026-09-14) raised the accepted source limit to 100 MP, so a 64 MP photo passes without being resized (it would only 413 above 100 MP).

Two things to weigh before deleting the step:

1. The guard, not the whole step. Grep shows nothing else in the repo enforces a source limit, so if you just delete prepare(), a future 100+ MP source goes straight at the API and comes back as a 413 at upload time. The minimal change is to raise the constant and keep the guard:

   MAX_SOURCE_PIXELS = 100_000_000  # Tamberline rejects larger sources (v2.6+)

2. The 8000 px output cap is unchanged, so dropping the downscale probably buys no visible quality. 64 MP at 3:2 is ~9798x6532, at 4:3 ~9238x6928 — both exceed 8000 px on the long side, so Tamberline's rendition is capped either way. Only near-square 64 MP shots (8000x8000) would land exactly at the cap. What you do get from dropping it is bigger uploads, slower prepares, and more bandwidth on every photo, for no rendition gain in the common aspect ratios.

So: allowed, yes. Worth it, probably not for image quality — the real motivations would be avoiding a lossy resize on near-square images or simplifying the pipeline. If you want, I can make the one-line constant change so the pipeline stops downscaling but still guards against >100 MP.

One caveat I can't verify from the repo: nothing pins an API or account version, so I'm assuming the account actually runs v2.6. Worth confirming the version your key resolves to before relying on 100 MP.
